key_insight: Predicting a good simplex warm start is not enough: the cheapest start is not always the one closest to optimal, so the start policy should be chosen using measured solver cost.
engineering_relevance: A cost-aware warm-start policy can cut linear-program solve time substantially in practice, making simplex more competitive for large LP pipelines.
method: Train a supervised model to predict an optimal basis from LP structure.
Use measured CPU instruction counts to learn when to warm-start, how many predicted columns to include, and which simplex variant/pricing rule to use.
Select the start policy per LP with a small learned controller instead of relying only on basis overlap or iteration counts.
evidence_signal: Across 25 LP classes, the proposed CostStart roughly halves solve time versus the default start and beats retrained published baselines by about 1.4× to 2.2×, including on LPs four times larger than training instances.
watch_item: The gains depend on solver-specific cost measurements and careful retraining, so deployment may require re-tuning for a different simplex implementation or hardware stack.
paper_title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
